summary.text: Tano Tijerina, a Republican and the Webb County Judge since 2015, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Texas's 28th District to Henry Cuellar.
A former minor league baseball player and rancher, he was elected county judge as a Democrat and switched to the Republican Party in December 2024.
He won the March 2026 Republican primary and campaigned on border security, affordability and public safety.

paragraphs.text: Tijerina earned a bachelor's degree in fitness and sports from Texas A&M International University.
He played minor league baseball and worked in the ranching industry before his judgeship, and Ballotpedia also lists him as executive vice president of the Precept Ministries Spanish Board.

Tijerina was elected Webb County Judge in 2014 as a Democrat and took office in 2015. He won re-election in 2018 with 76.3% against Republican Alfonso Casso and again in 2022, when no general election was held after he advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed.
In December 2024 he switched to the Republican Party, saying, according to the Texas Tribune, that the Democratic Party no longer aligned with his values.
He says his record as county judge includes cutting property taxes five times, delivering $20 million in utility relief, and expanding healthcare access in Webb County.
Tijerina announced his campaign for Congress on December 2, 2025; his third term as county judge runs through December 31, 2026.
He won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 74.3% of the vote over Eileen Day.
He received 29.6% of the vote to Henry Cuellar's 65.8%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
